title: Azure Application Gateway and WAF Health

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.2.46 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.2.46 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:diagnostics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="ApplicationGatewayAccessLog"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.46_azure_application_gatewa_46"
| sort -_time
description: Application Gateway is the primary L7 load balancer for most Azure web workloads. Backend health probe failures cause 502 errors for users; WAF blocks need tuning to avoid false positives.
value: Detecting azure application gateway and waf health early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable diagnostics on Application Gateway to send access logs and WAF logs via Event Hub or Storage Account to Splunk. Monitor backend pool health probe status from metrics (`UnhealthyHostCount`). Alert on rising 502/504 rates, unhealthy backends, and WAF blocks that correlate with user-reported issues. Track WAF rule hit distribution to tune rule exclusions.
visualization: Line chart (request rate and error rate), Table (unhealthy backends), Bar chart (WAF blocks by rule ID).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: This pattern can surge during change windows, in sandboxes, and when a platform is in maintenance, so we line alerts up with the calendar and take a second look before we call it an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) with the modular input for `azure:diagnostics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable diagnostics on Application Gateway to send access logs and WAF logs via Event Hub or Storage Account to Splunk. Monitor backend pool health probe status from metrics (`UnhealthyHostCount`). Alert on rising 502/504 rates, unhealthy backends, and WAF blocks that correlate with user-reported issues. Track WAF rule hit distribution to tune rule exclusions.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:diagnostics" Category="ApplicationGatewayAccessLog"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.46_azure_application_gatewa_46"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:diagnostics` in `index=cloud` to detect azure application gateway and waf health. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_46_alert` with severity aligned to `critical` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (request rate and error rate), Table (unhealthy backends), Bar chart (WAF blocks by rule ID)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics/diagnostics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure application gateway and waf health so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
